source.title: Dynamic Relative Representations for Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications
source.authors: S. Fiorellino; C. Battiloro; E. Strinati; P. Di Lorenzo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies relative representations to zero-shot stitching across pretrained encoders in a semantic-communications setting and reports results on that task; it does not test convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates zero-shot stitching performance across encoders and anchor-set cardinalities (Fig. 2), and states that absolute-representation stitching often fails. It does not directly measure representation-distance convergence. Results on resource allocation in Figs. 3–4 do not bear on the claim. Cited findings are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: Fig. 2 reports zero-shot stitching accuracy for five ImageNet encoders into a relative decoder trained on mobilenetv3_large_100. This bears on V4 via relative representations. The plotted values cannot be read from the supplied text, and the paper's main contribution is resource allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that relative representations enable zero-shot stitching across diverse pretrained encoders. They also conclude that their Lyapunov-based dynamic allocation achieves a favorable energy–delay–accuracy trade-off. Future work is optimal anchor and similarity-function selection.
record.recipe_differences: This is a semantic-communications application of anchor-based relative representations, using cosine similarity and randomly selected training-set anchors; it does not measure the original claim's scale-dependent representational convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Anchor-set cardinality is varied in Fig. 2, but the plotted values are not available in the supplied text. Cosine similarity is used without comparison to other similarity measures.
record.problems: Fig. 2 values and anchor cardinalities are not recoverable from the supplied text, and no uncertainty is stated for those results. The stitching evaluation is on CIFAR-10 with six listed pretrained encoders and a relative decoder trained using one frozen encoder.
record.rows_left_out: Resource-allocation results in Figs. 3–4 are omitted because they concern power, latency, and inference accuracy rather than representation alignment or interchangeability.

untested.parts: Linear maps, layer stitching and unpaired-data mapping. Also the size of the stitching loss relative to end-to-end, which is in Fig. 2 only and unreadable here.
Whether alignment changes with encoder size, even though encoders span 1.5M–98M parameters.
Only cosine similarity and random anchors are used. No metric or out-of-distribution comparison.

missing.what: Per-encoder stitching accuracy versus anchor cardinality, compared with the end-to-end dashed line. These values are needed to judge 'little loss' for V4.
Long-term accuracy targets up to 0.9 on CIFAR-10 are reported as met using the encoder set via RelReps. This is indirect evidence that stitched encoders retain accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is given for V4. Every stitching row is figure-only and cannot be read, so whether stitching loss is small cannot be checked. The authors only state that other encoders 'demonstrate zero-shot stitching capabilities'. The relative-representation method follows Moschella et al. [14]; this study applies it in semantic communications, close to a T4 use.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether alignment between independently trained models rises with size or capability.
No paired image-caption or vision-language alignment test.
No same-architecture, different-initialization feature or subspace comparison.
Tests relative-representation stitching only; does not test linear maps, layer stitching, unpaired-data mapping, or quantify loss relative to end-to-end performance.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Varies anchor-set cardinality for task performance, but does not measure convergence under different similarity measures or inputs, or test out-of-distribution data.
Does not determine whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

relation.reason: The study evaluates five alternative encoders with relative decoders trained using frozen mobilenetv3_large_100 representations; this directly bears on V4.

tranche.reason: Fig. 2 evaluates cross-encoder zero-shot stitching in a semantic-communications setting, providing a result relevant to V4 beyond resource-allocation performance.

source_check.notes: Fig. 2 numerical results are unavailable in the supplied text, so loss relative to end-to-end performance cannot be quantified. The text defines classification performance using validation accuracy in Eq. (4); the supplied manuscript is v3, dated 9 April 2025.
